questions.explanation: 'Tend to' softens a generalization: 'tend to stay up late'.
The sentence adverb 'Apparently' hedges the claim.
'Seem' takes 'to + infinitive': 'seems to be tired'.
options: He is seeming to be tired.

questions.explanation: 'Appear to' hedges a conclusion: 'appear to confirm'.
The adverb 'arguably' softens the claim.
questions.q: Smoking ___ increases the risk of cancer.

questions.explanation: 'May' hedges the prediction instead of stating certainty.
questions.q: It ___ rain later, so take an umbrella.

questions.explanation: 'Suggest' (singular subject) hedges a conclusion: 'The data suggests'.
questions.q: The data ___ that prices will rise.

questions.explanation: 'A bit of a' hedges a description: 'a bit of a perfectionist'.
'Presumably' marks the reason as an assumption, not a fact.
questions.q: ___ , he left because of the argument.

questions.explanation: 'Be likely to + infinitive' hedges a prediction.
options: The storm is likely hitting tonight.
The storm likely to hit tonight.
The storm is likely to hit tonight.
The storm is likely hit tonight.

questions.explanation: 'Could' hedges the claim instead of asserting certainty.
'Tend to' softens a general pattern.
The hedging adverb is 'largely': 'largely disproved'.
'Seem' agrees with the singular subject: 'She seems to enjoy'.
'Tend to' takes the bare infinitive: 'tends to arrive late'.
options: The results appear to be conclusive.
questions.q: Find the sentence with a mistake.

questions.explanation: 'Seem to' hedges with singular agreement: 'The evidence seems to suggest'.
'Kind of' hedges the adjective: 'kind of nervous'.
questions.q: He's ___ of nervous about the interview.

questions.explanation: The hedging adverb is 'somewhat': 'somewhat predictable'.
'Indicates' plus 'possible' hedges the claim most cautiously.
options: The report indicates to a decline.
The report certainly indicates a decline.
The report indicates that a decline.
The report indicates a possible decline.

questions.explanation: The sentence adverb 'Generally speaking' hedges the judgment.
